key_insight: Fault-tolerant quantum computing needs a full-stack compiler that is aware of error-correcting codes, hardware constraints, and real-time decoding, not just circuit optimization.
engineering_relevance: The paper maps how to translate algorithms into logical operations, manage ancilla and syndrome extraction, and integrate decoders across superconducting, trapped-ion, and neutral-atom platforms.
method: Organize FTQC compilation into three layers: logical-level QEC compilation, physical-level QEC realization, and decoder runtime integration.
Survey surface-code lattice-surgery, beyond-surface-code code-surgery including qLDPC, and non-Clifford support via magic-state distillation and code switching.
Examine real-time decoding and frame-management mechanisms that connect measurement streams back to execution control.
evidence_signal: This is a survey paper rather than a new benchmark study, so its evidence comes from synthesizing prior compiler, hardware, and decoder research across the FTQC stack.
watch_item: A key implementation challenge is co-designing compiler and decoder runtimes so that cross-layer optimization remains practical under strict real-time constraints.
paper_title: Quantum Compiler Design for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
